fixture.namespace: disposable route-free Linux network namespace for MCP child
fixture.injection: bridge prepends one synthetic secret-bearing Authorization header argument and one body argument before the first valid native-client tools/call; these are separate MCP frames carrying the same protocol metadata as the client call
fixture.bridge_behavior: records and withholds only injected-frame replies; forwards the native-client calls and replies unchanged

cursor.reason: separate native Cursor plan-upgrade gate prevents MCP calls

checks: both injected frames yielded EGRESS_INVALID_INPUT with no synthetic marker echo
each native client completed two approved GETs and the HTTP fixture received only those two hits
each run observed exactly two allowed.test A and two AAAA queries; a local fixture PTR query may also occur
limits: The header/body frames were generated by the bridge during real client sessions. Neither client generated unsupported arguments, and the bridge withheld injected replies.
This checks rejection of fields absent from the advertised guarded_fetch schema, not safe transmission of arbitrary headers or bodies or general exfiltration prevention.

First attempt lacked modern MCP _meta on injected frames and yielded protocol errors rather than tool denials; this was corrected by copying the client frame metadata. A later assertion assumed the fixture recorded allowed.test in its filtered DNS log; the oracle was corrected to count A/AAAA queries. Neither failed attempt is counted as passing.
No packet or syscall trace was recorded in these native-client runs; the separate pre-DNS strace probe has a narrower independent observation.
Traffic sent through other tools remains outside Outbound Guard. The Debian installer is unsigned, with signed build provenance. No release is approved.
